A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WD/WD-R study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and the addition of Appendix H.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and compression experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and a human study comprising 39,320 pairwise ratings.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime optimization results and a spatial splat-allocation analysis.

M1.justification: The objectives and core 3DGS procedure remain unchanged. However, Appendix A.1 introduces concrete computational optimizations: caching ground-truth VGG features/statistics and skipping zero-weight pyramid levels. Unlike v1's suggested future optimizations, v2 reports their implementation, preserving bit-exact loss values and gradients.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 21 scenes from Mip-NeRF 360, Deep Blending, Tanks & Temples, and BungeeNeRF, covering reconstruction and compression. The new Barcelona density analysis uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including Pixel-GS, Perceptual-GS, and the original framework objectives. The new density analysis uses original 3DGS as its comparator. Histogram panels omitted from the main-text display remain in Appendix G.

E3.justification: New Appendix H specifies an additional analysis protocol: project Gaussian centers into each view, retain centers inside the image, and accumulate opacity in 2×2-pixel bins. Existing training budgets, datasets, perceptual metrics, and human-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a Barcelona case study examining spatial allocation of splat capacity through density heatmaps and per-view counts, plus a runtime assessment of implementation optimizations. Existing loss-weight and pooling-size ablations, artifact examples, and effective-rank analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same human-study counts, Bayesian Elo aggregation, and 95% confidence-interval reporting. No new repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting procedure accompanies the added runtime and density results.

E6.justification: All ten table bodies are identical. v2 additionally reports approximately 48% lower WD per-iteration time after optimization and relative training overhead decreasing from approximately 4.5× to 2.8×. Appendix H reports approximately 10% more visible splats per Barcelona view despite fewer total splats, alongside the new spatial-allocation finding.

T1.justification: The objectives, WD distance, and effective-rank mathematics remain unchanged. WD/WD-R equations move from Appendix A.2 into Section 3.1, while the added standard cross-entropy expression explains the existing compression rate term. No new theoretical result, assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: perceptual improvement through loss replacement, the large human study, generalization across frameworks, and approximately 50% compression savings. The principal preference claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies sigma=4 as specific to the tested resolutions rather than universally optimal and proposes resolution-aware evaluation. It adds an interpretation of more view-relevant capacity allocation and explicitly characterizes the geometric analyses as post-hoc observations rather than causal explanations.

D1.justification: v2 documents caching, pyramid pruning, the 20 contributing levels out of 96, and density-map construction. Conversely, it removes the direct repository link and the explicit 0.8/0.2 original-loss coefficients while retaining the project-page link. This changes documented access information without establishing that actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and research positioning are retained. Bibliographic shortening and additional references to already cited work do not introduce new prior work or change the novelty claim.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory and wording edits, relocates loss formulas into the main text, shortens the compression discussion, corrects CMMD's expansion, and updates author/contact notes. Appendix H is added, while the established section ordering and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: A substantially narrower page design rescales and redistributes figures and tables throughout. v1 Figures 7–8 become panels of v2 Figure 5, the main effective-rank display is reduced to two retained methods, and density heatmaps appear in Figures 10 and 20. These are extensive display and layout changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens the paper through concrete runtime optimization evidence, a documented spatial-allocation analysis, and clearer qualifications about pooling scale and causal interpretation. The core experimental evidence is unchanged. Removing the direct repository link and explicit original-loss coefficients partly offsets these gains, limiting the overall improvement.
